title: The federal minimum wage reaches $17 in five annual steps from January 1, 2030
status: decided, memo 1 part 1 B
parameters: 29 U.S.C. 206(a)(1) is amended to $9.50 an hour on January 1, 2030, then $11.00 (2031), $12.50 (2032), $14.00 (2033), $15.50 (2034) and $17.00 (January 1, 2035), Raise the Wage's schedule [EV-WRK-042]. If the act is signed after June 30, 2029, the first step is the first January 1 at least six months after signature and each later step moves with it (working choice). A step may wait a year under the recession pause (LAB-4.03); the floor never falls. States and cities keep higher floors (29 U.S.C. 218, unchanged). A full-time worker at $17 earns $35,360 a year (project arithmetic, 2,080 hours)
current_law: $7.25 since July 24, 2009 [EV-WRK-002]; 20 states at $7.25 [EV-WRK-013]

title: From 2036, the floor rises each year with the median wage
status: decided, memo 1 part 1 B; the measure and timing are working choices
parameters: From January 1, 2036 (the year after the last step), the floor rises each January 1 by the percentage growth of the national median hourly wage over the latest year of published data, rounded up to the next $0.05; it never falls, and a year in which the median falls leaves it unchanged. *Measure (working choice):* BLS's all-occupation median hourly wage from the Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics survey, the measure memo 1 benchmarks against ($24.51 in May 2025) [EV-WRK-078]. The Secretary publishes the new rate by October 1 for the following January. The commission (LAB-4.04) may recommend a different BLS median by report; changing the measure needs a vote. On 3.5% a year median growth (range 3-4%), the floor stays near half the all-jobs median: about $17.60 in 2036 (project arithmetic)

title: A recession pause written into the schedule
status: decided, memo 1 part 2 (B within C); the date of the test is a working choice
parameters: On October 1 before each scheduled step (LAB-4.01), the Secretary checks the national unemployment rate: if its three-month average (seasonally adjusted) is at least 0.5 percentage point above its lowest three-month average in the preceding 12 months, the trigger shape in the 2025 UI bill [EV-WRK-395], the next step waits one year and every later step moves back a year. The check is repeated the next October 1. Indexing from 2036 (LAB-4.02) is not paused: it follows wages, which a recession already slows. The floor never falls. *Why:* the one finding of recession job loss is the 2007-09 federal steps [EV-WRK-064]; Dube's review recommends a mandate to pause [EV-WRK-052]. No trigger of this kind has been evaluated

title: A small, temporary payroll credit for employers under 50 workers in the first three steps
status: decided, memo 1 part 2 C, its form `DEC-2026-11-17-34`; the shares and cap are working choices
parameters: A refundable credit against the employer's share of payroll tax, claimed on the quarterly Form 941. *Who:* an employer with fewer than 50 employees in the prior calendar year, counted across a controlled group (26 U.S.C. 414(b), (c), (m), (o)) so a large firm cannot split. *What:* for each worker paid below a new step's rate in the quarter before the step, a share of the added wage cost (the new rate less the worker's old hourly wage, times hours paid) for the four quarters after the step: 50% in the first step's year, 35% in the second and 20% in the third (working choice). *Cap:* $20,000 per employer per year (working choice), so the credit stays inside the decided range. *Ends* after the third step's year: wages paid after December 31, 2032 on the working timeline (later if the pause, LAB-4.03, delays a step). *Contingent:* it pays only for steps the labor act enacts, as the legacy credit was designed [EV-WRK-703]. Cost about $0.02-0.04 trillion over FY2030-39 by memo 1's judgment (a third of the legacy credit's range); section 6 prices the credit as specified here at about $3 billion (range $1.5-7 billion), provisional, for Espen (6-cost.md, parts 1 and 4); JCT scores it (point 15). It replaces the budget model's LAB-5 row ($0.10 trillion) at booking, not here. *The 2007 package* (P.L. 110-28) is a political precedent, not evidence that a credit softens job effects (`notes/espen-questions-2026-11-17.md`, part a)

title: A union is certified on a majority of signed cards
status: decided, memo 3 D (card check)
parameters: 29 U.S.C. 159 is amended: when a union shows the Board valid authorization cards signed by a majority of the employees in an appropriate unit, the Board certifies it as the bargaining representative without an election. *Cards:* signed or electronically signed within the 12 months before the filing, naming the union and the wish to be represented (working choice). *Check:* the Board compares the cards with the employer's payroll list for the unit within 14 days of filing (working choice); the employer may not demand an election. *Unit disputes* go to the Board's expedited hearing; a dispute over a few names does not delay certification if the majority holds without them (working choice).
